sekcje: Drug Levels and Effects > Summary of Use during Lactation

A pharmacokinetic analysis found low levels of cabotegravir in breastmilk with maternal use of long-acting cabotegravir. Maintaining viral suppression with antiretroviral therapy decreases breastfeeding transmission risk to less than 1%, but not zero. Individuals with HIV who are on antiretroviral therapy with a sustained undetectable viral load and who choose to breastfeed should be supported in this decision. If a viral load is not suppressed, banked pasteurized donor milk or formula is recommended. Extended postnatal prophylaxis of breastfed infants with cabotegravir should continue until breastfeeding is stopped.
Drug Levels and Effects > Drug Levels

Maternal Levels. An abstract reports a study in which long-acting cabotegravir 600 mg was injected intramuscularly every 56 days to 27 nursing mothers. Median breastmilk concentrations at these times were 14.6 mcg/L just before the 1-month injection, 29.8 mcg/L one week later, 27.4 mcg/L just before the 5-month injection, and 36.1 mcg/L one week later.
Infant Levels. Relevant published information was not found as of the revision date.
